title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-09
content:
2026-03-04 - quick personal scratchpad (GPU ops / capacity)

TL;DR
- Follow ups for p3 cluster: investigate noisy neighbor on node gpu-08, schedule maintenance window for driver update, and run autoscaler stress test this week.

Morning checks (done)
- Cluster health OK except gnode-08 high GPU mem usage spikes (~22:10 UTC last night).
- Alert INFRA-342 fired 3x between 22:00-23:30 (trace attached in JIRA).
- Metrics: avg token/sec per GPU down ~12% on p3-west due to smaller batch sizes on recent rollout.

Immediate TODOs (priority order)
1) Investigate noisy neighbor gnode-08 (priority: high)
   - ssh -> /var/log/nvidia/gpu-manager.log (grep highmem)
   - check cgroup attribution for pods on that node (kubectl top/pods, describe)
   - coordinate with Marco if we need to cordon + drain (expect 15-20m disruption for that host)
   - link: JIRA INFRA-342 (assigned to Marco, need more logs)
2) Driver update window (priority: med)
   - Kernel + nvidia-driver 535.x patch tested on staging last week, no regressions on quantized models.
   - Need to book 2h maintenance for p3-west (low traffic window: Sat 03:00-05:00 UTC).
   - Notify #infra and customer-success by EOD Wed.
3) Autoscaler stress test (priority: med)
   - Run scale-to-zero -> burst-to-50 test on dedicated test pool.
   - Steps: generate 10k short requests (script: infra/tools/loadgen/run_burst.sh)
   - Measure cold start latency, queue depth, successful fallbacks to lower-tier models.
4) Batching profile tweak (priority: low)
   - Try increased batching window from 8ms -> 12ms for chat workloads in p3-west; simulate with replay tool.
   - Note: might slightly increase P99 but reduce per-token cost.

Notes / observations
- Saw increased 4xx errors for model-rerank on 2026-03-03 21:40 UTC; suspected upstream network flaps. File: /var/log/servertunnel/error-20260303.log
- KV cache hit rate for embedding flow is stable (~82%) but some spike on one customer route - follow up with SRE to check route-level caching TTL.
- Consider adding an alert for sustained batch size < 2 for CPU-backed endpoints (indicates bad client retry pattern).

Commands / quick references
- Check node gpu mem: ssh ops@gpu-08 sudo journalctl -u nvidia* --since "2 hours ago"
- Drain node: kubectl cordon gpu-08 && kubectl drain gpu-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Restart driver: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver && sudo reboot (only after window)

Follow-ups / questions for the week
- @Jia: can you run a longer replay for low-latency chat profile with the new batching params? update test matrix when done.
- @Marco: if we end up replacing the host, what's our expected reprovision time? need to capture spare-GPU SLA for capacity planning.
- Procurement: request quote for 4x spare A100 cards to keep in rotation (cc: finance)

Random scratch ideas (unpolished)
- Metric: add per-model rolling avg of tokens/sec per GPU + estimated $/1000 tokens to console (quick view for cost SLOs).
- Small experiment: local on-node caching layer for prefix-heavy chat to reduce KV desyncs across shards.

End of day checklist
- [ ] Post maintenance announcement if driver window confirmed
- [ ] Attach logs and initial investigation notes to INFRA-342
- [ ] Schedule autoscaler stress test and add results to PR 881 (serving-runtime)

Notes to self: keep this short, move polished runbook into confluence after we confirm steps.
